chunks: And by his chain, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

What God had obligated upon the servants from salat was ten rak'at, and in them is recitation, and there is no doubt (i.e., inadvertent mistake) in them. Then the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) added seven, and in them is doubt (allowed), and there is no recitation in them.

key_terms.السهو: al-sahw — inadvertent forgetfulness or mistake during prayer
key_terms.الصلاة: salat — the prescribed daily ritual prayer
key_terms.القراءة: al-qira'a — recitation of Quran, obligatory in the first two rak'at
key_terms.الوهم: al-wahm — doubt about the number of rak'at performed; gives rise to sujud al-sahw
key_terms.ركعات: rak'at — individual units/cycles of the prayer
key_terms.فرض: fard — what is divinely obligated, as opposed to what is added by prophetic authority

ai.seo_question: Why are there different rules for recitation and doubt in the different units of the daily prayers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) explains the legislative history of the daily prayers. The original divine obligation was ten rak'at requiring Quranic recitation and admitting no inadvertent mistakes. The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) then added seven rak'at (the additional units in Dhuhr, Asr, Isha, and Maghrib), in which doubt about the number of rak'at is accommodated by prostrations of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw), but in which recitation is not required — only tasbeeh. This hadith establishes the Prophetic origin of the nafilah-like structure of these extra rak'at and the rules distinguishing them from the original ten.
